# H8 — 1.0 public candidacy (D4-conditional)

**Mission** — Make `github.com/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit` mechanically ready to be a public 1.0: every exported symbol documented, every public claim in README/docs backed by a checkable anchor, the repo's own guardrails run against the repo itself, and a written compatibility promise whose coverage is enforced by `constitution-lint` — so that a stranger cloning the repo inherits the same "every claim checked against ground truth" discipline the kit sells. The work is split so that most of it is pure private hygiene with standing value even if Geoff vetoes going public.

**Repos & write scope** — Writes ONLY to `/Volumes/m2ext/code/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit`. `../sextant`, `../throughline`, `../growing-gardens-bi` are READ-ONLY grounding. GitHub repo settings (visibility flip) are Geoff's action, never the team's.

**Trigger** — Two-stage. **Stage A (hygiene): ready now** — it is exactly the work D4 already named: *"Everything in this plan (org-agnostic scrub, honest ledger, mechanical constitution) is also exactly the public-readiness work"* (docs/plans/2026-07-uplift.md §3 D4). **Stage B (publication): BLOCKED until D4 is ratified YES.** Verify before building Stage B: the Wave-4 item *"[~] D4 revisited: public/1.0 decision … decision is Geoff's"* (docs/plans/2026-07-uplift.md, Wave 4, line ~360) must be flipped to a recorded YES by Geoff in that file, TRACKING.md, or CHANGELOG.md (whose ~line 130 already records "Presented to owner with the v0.6.0 ledger. Decision is Geoff's" — a ratification may land there). If all still read `[~]`/undecided, build Stage A only and stop.

## Design constraints

- **Stdlib-only root module** — every new check/tool uses `go/ast`, `go/parser`, `os`, `path/filepath` only; `empty-require` lint already enforces the go.mod. No gitleaks/golangci binaries as required infrastructure, and **no required shell-out to `../sextant/bin/fathom`** — sibling binaries are absent in CI and a skip-if-absent path is vacuous-pass theater.
- **Extend, don't fork, constitution-lint**: new checks follow the exact `func checkX(root string) []Finding` + `checks`-slice + `testdata/` fixture shape in `cmd/constitution-lint/main.go`; waiver files follow the `waivers.txt` format (path per line, `#` comments, reason required).
- **Org-agnostic even in the linter**: denylist and secret-scan patterns are config data (`org-denylist.txt`, pattern file), never Go literals.
- **Honest non-guarantees**: threat-model.md and SECURITY.md may only restate what tests prove; VISION belief 6 wording is the ceiling. Overclaiming in a public-facing doc is this spec's worst possible defect.
- **CUE owns shape** — n/a here (no new data-shaped packages); do NOT invent a schema.cue for docs.
- **Docs-as-claims**: anything checkable goes into docs/plans/public-readiness.md anchors, not prose assertions; non-code deliverables that no lint proves go in CHANGELOG, never as symbol-less claims.
- Injected clocks / concurrency-contract doc comments apply to any new package (cmd/release-notes is a process-lifetime CLI: state "not safe for concurrent use; single-shot CLI" honestly).

## Acceptance = proof (machine-checkable only)

- `task validate` green (includes the extended `constitution-lint` — so A2/A3/A4/A5a/B3 self-prove: the gate fails if any classification/doc/org/secret hit is unfixed and unwaived).
- `go run ./cmd/constitution-lint -v` lists the new checks passing by name.
- `gofmt -l` empty on touched files; `go test -race` on `cmd/constitution-lint`, `cmd/release-notes` green; `TestSecretScanCanary` passes and fails when the canary pattern is removed (verify by temporary mutation in review, not committed); `TestFirstAgentWalkthrough` green (mock-mode output matches docs/first-agent.md's fenced block) and fails when the doc's expected block is mutated.
- README package count matches `docs/catalog.md`'s generated total; `task docs-index` produces no diff (`catalog-fresh` green).
- `docs/plans/public-readiness.md` passes the pre-push fathom-verify gate — every claim symbol-anchored per the A7 grammar rules (or, if H1 hasn't landed and the bug reproduces, carries the documented bug note + hand-verification record per A7).
- PR summary reports the stable/experimental/internal-ish classification counts and the doc-waiver count.
- TRACKING.md + CHANGELOG.md updated in the same change as each landing; `task downstream-check` green (growing-gardens-bi's go.mod fix is already applied despite TRACKING's stale `[~]`; lint additions must not break sextant/throughline builds — they don't compile the linter, but run it anyway).
- Stage B only: dry-run tag proves release.yml (with `contents: write`) produces a Release whose body equals `cmd/release-notes` output for that tag, with the run URL + body hash recorded in docs/plans/public-readiness.md before cleanup; nested-module `go.mod` requires point at a real tag (grep proves no `v0.0.0` remains).

## Non-goals & theater traps

- **Do NOT rebuild what exists**: LICENSE exists; CI (`ci.yml`) exists and already closes the cue-vet skip hole; tag discipline exists; `docs/first-agent.md` exists (fix drift, don't rewrite); the org-agnostic *scrub* was already done in the uplift — A4 makes it *mechanical*, it is not a from-scratch hunt; `catalog-fresh` already prevents catalog drift — don't add a second catalog mechanism.
- **Do NOT flip repo visibility, create the v1.0.0 tag, or publish to pkg.go.dev** — those are Geoff's actions after B4.
- **Do NOT add a `/v1` module path suffix** — Go doesn't require it and it would break all three downstream consumers.
- Theater traps: (1) a doc-coverage check with a waiver file containing half the tree — every waiver needs a stated reason and the count goes in the PR summary; (2) a threat-model that quietly upgrades "defense-in-depth" to "boundary" — diff it against VISION belief 6; (3) a secret scan with no planted-positive, or one whose scanner is a sibling binary that's absent in CI so the canary skips — an all-clear from an unproven or un-run scanner is the exact ABSENT_PROVEN failure D10 names; (4) marking public-readiness claims `[x]` while relying on the known-broken fathom `verify` to "pass" via `FATHOM_BIN=/nonexistent` without the hand-verification record; (5) fixing README's "148" to a new literal — it drifts again; generate or lint it; (6) 174 rows all stamped `experimental` sails through compat-coverage — the counts in the PR summary plus Geoff's sign-off are the backstop; (7) a dry-run tag deleted with no recorded run URL/body hash — unre-checkable proof is not proof.
